messages:
lia: Heads-up — saw a ~15% P99 token latency regression on the loRA-7B workload after yesterday's runtime change (batching + kernel selection). traces attached (nsys + perfetto).
ryan: ugh. which CL/sha?
lia: CL 4821 / sha abc1234. change was: prefer_early_handoff=true and kernel-selector: prefer_fused=false for short tails. baseline was prefer_early_handoff=false, prefer_fused=true.
devon: any evidence the kernel selector actually chose a different kernel?
lia: yes — nsys timeline shows fused_attn_bf16 almost gone on the bad run; instead we get gemm_generic + aten_attn fallback. sample from the nsys summary: 
```
# bad run (abc1234) top kernels (by time):
gemm_generic     42.1%  1.23s
aten_attn_fallback  21.3%  0.62s
kv_cache_lookup   4.5%   0.13s
fused_attn_bf16   1.2%   0.04s
```
```
# good run (pre-4821) top kernels:
fused_attn_bf16   45.0%  1.10s
gemm_optimized    18.0%  0.44s
kv_cache_lookup   2.1%   0.05s
```
lia: also saw KV cache miss rate jump in the runtime logs: 3.2% -> 12.1% which increases decoder token work.
marta: that KV jump could explain it — more KV misses => longer seqs into slower kernels. do we have traces that align kv miss events with kernel handoffs?
devon: perfetto flame shows KV lookup spikes right before gemm_generic bursts. attached a perfetto timeline png in thread.
lia: repro steps I used (short):
```
# run harness
./bench/regen_workload --model lora-7b --seq 1024 --batch 4 --tokens 20000 --profile nsys --out out_bad.nsys
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -o out_bad out_bad.nsys
```
ryan: can we bisect quickly? I can spin the bisect script onto the dedicated cluster, but need a deterministic perf test and a build script.
marta: I put a small bisect wrapper in ci: scripts/bisect_perf.sh that builds and runs the harness and heuristically decides good/bad from median P99.
lia: posted good/bad traces on S3: s3://redwood-perf/pre-4821-good.nsys and s3://redwood-perf/post-4821-bad.nsys.
devon: quick hypothesis: the change to prefer_fused=false added a safety check that incorrectly matched layer shapes as "short tail" and forced non-fused path for many key sizes. I saw selector logs like: `selected_kernel=gemm_generic reason=tail_estimate<8` — the tail_estimate looks off in the short-run config.
lia: exact selector log snippet (bad):
```
[selector] layer 12: seq_len=256 tail_estimate=6 selected=gemm_generic
[selector] layer 13: seq_len=256 tail_estimate=5 selected=gemm_generic
```
lia: (good run):
```
[selector] layer 12: seq_len=256 tail_estimate=256 selected=fused_attn_bf16
```
ryan: wow that tail_estimate difference is suspicious. Could be an integer/float truncation in the new heuristic.
marta: I'll run a narrow bisect: check 10 commits around 4821 and produce quick nsys lightweight profiles (1k tokens). gives a quick signal.
perf-bot: queued bisect job: commits range 4811..4831, harness=regen_workload, short-profile=1k tokens, analysis=median P99. job id perf-bot-8891.
devon: while bisect runs, can someone grep the selector change? I suspect a refactor where we switched a / operator to integer division on C++17 change.
lia: i already checked: line in kernel_selector.cpp changed `float tail = remaining / block;` -> `int tail = remaining / block;` in CL 4821.
ryan: that would do it. int truncation will undercount tail and force non-fused kernel.
marta: if bisect confirms, quick fix is to revert that line back to float or cast. but need to prove perf delta minimal after patch.
devon: also check that batching handoff (prefer_early_handoff) interacts — it shortens sequences seen by kernel selector and could amplify truncation.
lia: agreed. experiment matrix: (a) revert integer truncation, (b) keep truncation but set prefer_early_handoff=false, (c) both fixes.
lia: attaching the two short raw nsys files to S3 for anyone who wants to run `nsys stats` locally.
ryan: thanks — I'll prioritize the revert patch and run quick CI perf. if fixes show p99 back to baseline we'll ship a patch. feel free to ping me in thread. :thumbsup:
marta: running bisect now, will update with commit where metric flips.
perf-bot: bisect update: first midpoint 4816 -> test good (p99 ~ baseline).
perf-bot: bisect update: midpoint 4824 -> test bad (+14% p99).
perf-bot: bisect update: result points to 4821 as first bad commit.
lia: confirmed locally. reverting int truncation in kernel_selector.cpp and re-running short profile yields fused_attn_bf16 back in timeline and KV miss rate back to ~3.5%.
devon: thanks. can someone open a PR with the fix and a regression test (selector unit test covering tail calc) plus a perf smoke test?
ryan: i'll open the PR and link this thread + bisect traces. PR will include a small perf CI gate for loRA-7B.
lia: hugely relieved — nice catch. :partyparrot:
marta: note for postmortem: interaction between batching handoff and kernel selector heuristics (int/float math) — add a dedicated test for that interaction.
lia: I'll drop a short post in #incidents once PR merges so infra can redeploy and validate cluster latencies.
ryan: closing loop later today after deploy.
